title: Teaching the Gospel of Jesus Christ (Part 1)
focus: Practice topic: faith in Jesus Christ and repentance
intro: The gospel of Jesus Christ is how we come back to God. Its first principles are faith in Jesus Christ and repentance. In this lesson learners study how the Savior cleanses us and practise teaching these two principles.
preparation: Study Mosiah 3:19; 4:1–3; 5:2; and Alma 36. Prepare a picture of Alma the Younger’s conversion and a short video on the Savior as the way. Make a copy of the repentance handout for each learner. Pray for each learner by name.

sections.title: Cleansed through Christ
paras: Before class, write on the board: What does it mean to be clean? Let learners answer as they come in. Ask: What makes us unclean, and what do we need to draw closer to Jesus Christ?

Read the section on how we are cleansed through Christ and pull out these truths: God sent His Son so we could return. Only through the Savior’s grace and mercy can we be clean. No unclean thing can live in God’s presence. Christ stood in our place and suffered for our sins. He forgives us when we accept Him, repent and obey. Let each learner choose a verse that shows one of these truths and explain how they would use it with an investigator.

sections.title: Faith in Jesus Christ
paras: Ask: What is the difference between helping someone come unto Christ and helping someone join the Church? Why does the first matter more? Read the first paragraph on faith and ask learners what it means to have faith in Jesus Christ.

Write on the board: Faith in Jesus Christ leads to action. Ask what actions show an investigator is growing in faith, such as praying, reading, keeping commitments and changing habits. Ask learners to write in a journal how faith has moved them to act, and one more thing they can do. Pairs then prepare a two-to-three-minute lesson on faith in their own words, using one scripture.

sections.title: Repentance: turning back to God
paras: Show the picture of Alma and the sons of Mosiah. Tell how Alma remembered his father’s words about Jesus Christ, called on Him and was changed (see Alma 36:6–24). Read Alma 36:13, 17–21. Ask: How did Alma show faith? What came of it? What was the result of his repentance?

Give one minute to write a one-sentence definition of repentance. Let several read theirs. Share the idea from Elder Neil L. Andersen that repentance is a turning toward God. Write on the board: Repentance is turning back toward God. Study Mosiah 3:19; 4:1–3 and 5:2 and look for evidence that King Benjamin’s people had faith and repented. Ask learners to study the section on repentance and make a chart with three columns: what we do, what changes in us, and what we feel. Examples: recognize sins, confess and turn away; fresh view of self and God, a growing wish to follow Him; peace, forgiveness, joy.

Ask: How do the first and second columns help you explain repentance? Why must we first have faith in Christ for the third column to be real? Close by showing the video of a woman changed through repentance. Ask what proved that she had turned to God.

sections.title: Teaching it in a hard moment
paras: Set the scenario: two roommates. One feels weighed down by a mistake and thinks he cannot change. Pairs prepare to teach him that with the Savior’s help repentance is possible. Teachers use their own words, simple and clear, and kindly invite him to act.
The partner plays the roommate and gives real reactions. Afterward ask what felt sincere and what could be clearer.

steps.why: Teach the idea and why it matters for a missionary.

examples.title: Show the first principles
examples.text: Write faith and repentance on the board. Show one verse for each and explain in your own words why they come first.

examples.title: Draw the repentance chart
examples.text: Make the three-column chart on the board and ask learners to add one example under each column.

examples.title: Show Alma’s story
examples.text: Tell Alma 36:13, 17–21 in your own words. Show how faith led to repentance.

steps.why: Show one example of what learners will do.

examples.title: Teach faith in three minutes
examples.text: Define faith, show it leads to action, read one verse and invite a small step.

examples.title: Teach repentance to someone who feels stuck
examples.text: Show a kind way to say that change is possible with the Savior’s help.

examples.title: Teach with a story
examples.text: Use Alma’s story to teach repentance in your own words, and ask what Alma did first.

steps.why: Learners practise in pairs or small groups.

examples.title: Teach in pairs
examples.text: Pairs teach faith and repentance in six minutes with one scripture and a testimony.

examples.title: Role-play the roommate
examples.text: One plays a weighed-down roommate. The other teaches hope through repentance.

examples.title: Write a one-sentence definition
examples.text: Each learner writes and shares a simple definition of repentance.

steps.why: Name what went well and what can improve.

examples.title: Partner feedback
examples.text: The learner who was taught says what was clearest and what felt most sincere. The teacher writes one thing to keep and one to improve.

examples.title: Three questions
examples.text: Ask: What went well? What would you change? What helped the listener most to understand faith and repentance? Begin with the good.

examples.title: Simple checklist
examples.text: Was it simple? Was a scripture used and explained? Was the listener invited to act? Did the teacher speak with sincerity?

steps.why: Practise again with what was learned.

examples.title: Switch roles
examples.text: The learner who listened now teaches. Leave time for feedback both ways, then ask a few to share what they learned.

examples.title: Improve one thing
examples.text: Each learner teaches again and changes one thing from the feedback: a clearer sentence, a better scripture or a warmer invitation.

examples.title: Teach a new partner
examples.text: Find a new partner. Teach the same lesson again in a few minutes. Share one insight with the class.

testimony: Testify that the Savior forgives and that repentance brings joy. Share a time you felt His mercy.

tips.text: When a student gives an answer that is not quite right, thank them and ask the question another way.
Ask for a simple definition. If learners can say it simply, they understand it.
Let pairs prepare a short lesson, then ask them to give feedback.
Open each lesson with a picture or question that catches attention.

quote.text: We have no more disposition to do evil, but to do good continually.

study: Read Alma 36:17–20 together and ask what changed when Alma remembered the Savior.
invitations: Teach a family home evening lesson on faith in Jesus Christ.
Study the passages on faith in the manual’s scripture study box.
Use the Topical Guide and the words of living prophets to study repentance. Write what you learn.
Try to repent every day and record what you notice. Share the video on the Savior with a friend.

Welcome the class warmly. Begin with a prayer and a short thought from scripture to invite the Holy Ghost.
What happened when you tried last lesson’s invitation? Who would like to share?
Listen for: real experiences, effort made, one thing learned.
Try saying: “Before we start, who would like to tell us what happened when they tried last week’s invitation?”

parts.title: Teaching it in a hard moment

blocks.text: Rotate the roles after four minutes.
Set the scenario: two roommates. **One feels weighed down by a mistake and thinks he cannot change.**

Pairs prepare to teach him that with the Savior’s help repentance is possible.
How to run it: show one example first, then let pairs try it. Keep it to a few minutes and thank each learner.
Teachers use their own words, simple and clear, and kindly invite him to act. The partner plays the roommate and gives real reactions. Afterward ask what felt sincere and what could be clearer.
Listen for: hope, simplicity and an invitation.
Say: “You can change with the Savior’s help.”

assignments: Read Alma 36:17–20 again at home. Write one thing it teaches you and be ready to share it.
Practise this topic with someone at home before next class: faith in Jesus Christ and repentance.
